court_name: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT BOMBAY
petitioner: Giri Textiles, through Proprietor Chandrayya R. Pasnuri
respondent: Anthony Nadar And Jainam Silk Mills
government_department_involved: Labour Court, Thane, Industrial Court, Thane, Labour Office

directives.text: Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014 shall proceed before the Labour Court, Thane in accordance with law and be decided on its own merits, uninfluenced by any observations made in the impugned orders or in the present judgment, save and except on the issue concluded herein;
The Labour Court shall endeavour to dispose of the said application as expeditiously as possible and preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of this order;
directives.deadline_text: within a period of six months from the date of receipt of this order

raw_summary: The High Court of Bombay dismissed a writ petition by Giri Textiles, upholding the lower courts' decision regarding the maintainability of an application by respondent Anthony Nadar. The petitioner's objection, based on alleged non-compliance with an 'approach notice' under the Maharashtra Industrial Relations Act, was deemed hypertechnical due to the employer's lack of transparency in the employment relationship. The Labour Court is directed to proceed with and expeditiously dispose of the original application, preferably within six months.
